item.title: The Tree Trim Set — Red
item.description: Three name-drop ornaments, one coat, one box. $18 less than buying them one at a time. Three ornaments is the number that actually gets used. One for your tree, one for the box you hand someone in December, and one that ends up on a wreath or a gift you did not plan on giving. Each is the same metal ornament sold on its own at $29 — 3.5″ round white aluminium, printed both sides, red ribbon threaded through the hole. Three of them at list is $87. This is $69, and the $18 is the only argument the set needs to make. Pick one coat for all three, or give each ornament its own name at checkout. Per our print partner these three consolidate into one parcel because they are one product from one facility; that is the ornament economics we built the price on, and we will confirm it against our own first orders rather than ask you to take it on faith.

item.title: The Long Dog Gift Box — Red
item.description: Puzzle, mug and a coat sticker. $84 instead of $94, in up to 3 packages. The box you give someone who already has a dachshund and does not need another mug — except this is the mug with their actual dog on it, next to a puzzle that takes an evening and the sticker that ends up on their laptop. Three things that do different jobs. The puzzle is 252 pieces, 10.62″ × 13.62″ finished, and the name prints on the box lid rather than the picture. The mug is the wrap-around 11 oz we have been selling on its own. The sticker is 3″ kiss-cut vinyl in the same coat — and it is the one thing here you cannot buy by itself, because postage on a single sticker costs more than the sticker. Honest about the packaging: this ships in up to 3 packages . A ceramic mug, a boxed puzzle and a sheet of vinyl are made on different equipment, and per our print partner they are not guaranteed to leave together — we price for the worse case and tell you up front rather than let a half-empty box read as a missing item. Each parcel carries its own tracking, at no extra shipping cost to you, and all of it is covered by the same 5–11 business day window.

item.title: Name-Drop Ornament — Red
item.description: Your dog’s coat and your dog’s name, 3.5″ of metal, printed both sides. The $12 ornament at the supermarket has a generic dog on it. This one has your dog’s coat and Otto 2026 on it, which is the difference between a decoration and the thing that comes out of the box first every December. Personalized ornaments are the one category where the boutique price is not a guess — the same $24.95 holds across 26 competitor ornaments we measured, and $29 buys a two-sided metal print rather than a flat printed disc. 3.5″ round white aluminium, 0.025″ thick, glossy, with the image on both faces and a red ribbon threaded through the hole at the top. Those are our print partner’s figures; we will confirm them against our own samples. Printed and packed in the USA.

item.title: Coat Portrait Mug — Red
item.description: Your exact dachshund, wrapped around a mug. Six coats, two sizes. The cheapest way to find out whether someone is a dachshund person: hand them this and watch them turn it around looking for their dog. They will find it. The Winston & Bear mug is $16.99 with a generic dachshund on it. This is your dog’s coat, optionally with his name, printed in the USA — and $34 is the observed category median of $35, so you are paying the market price rather than a premium for the word “custom”. The illustration uses the full wrap, which is the only honest way to print a dachshund on a cylinder — nose near the handle, body all the way round, tail arriving back where it started. A shorter dog would fit on one face. Yours does not, and that is the joke and the point. Glossy white ceramic. Per our print partner: 11 oz is 3.8″ tall and 3.2″ across, 15 oz is 4.7″ by 3.3″, both dishwasher- and microwave-safe. Printed and boxed in the USA in a moulded insert, because mugs that travel loose arrive as gravel.

item.title: The Long Dog Puzzle
item.description: 252 pieces of long dog. The name prints on the box lid, not the picture. A 252-piece puzzle is an evening with the family, not a mug. It is the one thing in this catalogue that takes three hours of someone’s attention rather than three seconds of recognition. The composition is landscape and uses all six coats at once, which is the only time the whole drawing system appears in one image. The name goes on a plate on the box lid rather than into the artwork — a name printed across a puzzle is a name cut into 252 pieces, and nobody wants that. Per our print partner: pressed paper chipboard 0.06″ thick, semi-gloss finish, 252 pieces assembling to 10.62″ × 13.62″ (27 × 34.6 cm), in a printed box. Made and boxed in the USA. Choking hazard — small parts, not for children under 3. An honest note on the price: we could not find a comparable dachshund puzzle anywhere in our competitor research, so $54 is anchored to the personalized-gift median of $49.99 in that data rather than to a puzzle we can point at. It is a larger, boxed object than that median item, and it is the only thing we sell with a name on the box lid. If you think that is wrong, tell us — hello@badgerandbone.com .

item.title: Coat Portrait Canvas — Red
item.description: A stretched canvas of your dog’s coat, 12×16 or 16×20, with the name if you want it. Crown & Paw wants $79.95 for a canvas. West & Willow’s median is $60 with most of its catalogue permanently on sale. The category p25 is $107 and the median $159.95 — so a $89 stretched canvas of your dog’s actual coat is the value option in a category that normally starts higher, which is an unusual sentence for us to be able to write. It arrives stretched on a wooden frame and ready to hang. 12×16 is the one most people put in a hallway or above a desk; 16×20 is for a wall that can carry it. The name is optional and sets below the dog in the same type as the prints. Text only — we do not accept photo uploads on anything we sell, here or elsewhere. A photo-upload business is a manual-retouching business, and we would rather sell you a drawing we can actually make well.

item.title: Pet-Paw Keepsake Ornament
item.description: A paw-shaped metal ornament, not a printed circle. Name and years if you want them. It is a paw-shaped die , not a printed circle. That is the visible reason this costs more than the round one, and it is the only reason we are offering. Per our print partner it is 3.5″ × 3.75″ aluminium at 0.04″ thick — noticeably heavier gauge than the 0.025″ round ornament — with a red ribbon and a hole to thread it through. Being straight with you about the price: at $36 this sits above the $17.50–$24.95 boutique ornament band we measured, further above it than our own pricing rule normally allows. We think the die shape carries it. If, when you have it in your hand, you think it does not, send it back inside 30 days and we will refund it — and tell us, because that is the kind of thing we would want to know.

item.title: Long Dog Mini Print
item.description: A 5×7 matte print. The small one you add to the order you were making anyway. This is the $24 thing you add to reach free shipping, and we are not going to pretend otherwise. It is also a real US-printed 5×7 on 189 g/m² matte stock rather than a $12.99 poster that arrives creased. It is the entry rung of the art ladder here — $24 mini print, $39 anatomy print, $89 canvas — and the one that fits on a desk without requiring a decision about the wall. The caption plate takes an optional name. Per our print partner the stock is 10.3 mil thick at 94% opacity, which in plain terms means it does not show what is behind it and it does not curl in a frame.
